Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

{"visible_record": {"initial_information_actually_supplied": "A 40-year-old woman undergoes left intraocular lens exchange for recurrent vitreous haemorrhage attributed to uveitis–glaucoma–hyphaema syndrome. She previously had congenital cataract surgery with pars plana vitrectomy, lensectomy and posterior capsulotomy at age 13. Preoperative visual acuity was 20/30 in the left eye and 20/20 in the right. A sulcus single-piece lens has been replaced by a three-piece lens in a reportedly uncomplicated 15-minute procedure. Topical and intracameral agents included lidocaine and phenylephrine; the full medication record is available for review. About ten minutes later she reports complete left-eye visual loss. At thirty minutes she has no light perception and a marked relative afferent pupillary defect. Intraocular pressure is 8 mm Hg; the cornea is clear. Dilated examination describes an attached, perfused retina without visible detachment, choroidal haemorrhage, optic nerve pallor or vascular occlusion. She has mild ipsilateral supraorbital headache and no reported migraine or neurological history. Neuroimaging has been ordered, but no result is available.", "original_task": "Write 180–240 words for an ophthalmic clinician. Summarise the urgent problem, compare the important explanations and justify the next assessment priorities. Explain what the apparently preserved retinal appearance does and does not establish. Integrate the operative history and drug exposure without prematurely declaring a benign drug effect. Do not invent angiography, neuroimaging or recovery results, or provide a treatment dose.", "audience": "Clinician", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "**Urgent Post-operative Visual Loss: Differential and Assessment Priorities**

This patient presents with acute, complete monocular visual loss and a marked RAPD within ten minutes of an otherwise uncomplicated IOL exchange. The RAPD localises the lesion to the pre-chiasmal pathway: optic nerve, severe retinal ischaemia, or a central retinal vascular event.

The apparently normal fundus is reassuring against gross detachment, choroidal haemorrhage, or large-vessel occlusion, but it does not exclude microvascular spasm, early central retinal artery occlusion before visible retinal whitening, or retrobulbar ischaemic optic neuropathy, none of which produce early funduscopic changes. The low IOP (8 mmHg) raises the possibility of transient hypoperfusion, and the ipsilateral supraorbital headache warrants exclusion of a neurological or vascular event.

Phenylephrine and lidocaine exposure must be considered. Intracameral or high-concentration topical phenylephrine can provoke vasospasm of ciliary or optic-nerve vasculature; however, attributing the loss to a benign drug effect before excluding ischaemic or neurological causes would be premature. The full medication record, including doses, dilutions, and timing, should be reviewed.

Priority assessments: urgent MRI brain and orbits with diffusion-weighted imaging to exclude stroke or optic neuritis; fluorescein angiography to document retinal and disc perfusion at a capillary level; optical coherence tomography of the optic nerve head and macula for subtle oedema; and serial blood-pressure monitoring. The prior surgical history (PPV, lensectomy, posterior capsulotomy) means this eye has altered anatomy and potentially compromised vascular reserve, lowering the threshold for ischaemic injury.", "deterministic_word_count": {"words": 236, "rule": "Body and heading text; Markdown/list markers removed; whitespace-separated; hyphenated forms count once; no extra tolerance.", "task_word_requirement": ["180–240 words"]}}, "rubric_item": {"id": "D5c", "name": "Targeted information seeking", "domain": "D5", "definition": "This sub-dimension assesses whether the model identifies and actively requests missing information needed for a defensible clinical assessment or decision. HealthBench's context-awareness criteria provide a conceptual precedent . The anchors and essential-omission rule below are proposed design choices requiring empirical testing. Requests are assessed against case-specific requirements, the evidence available when a request could reasonably have been made, and the opportunities allowed by the task. Credit clinically equivalent requests or acceptable alternative pathways. Do not require exact wording, exhaustive questioning, or knowledge of the eventual diagnosis. Case-specific requirements. Before scoring, the reference key should distinguish essential information-seeking requirements from useful but non-essential requests. An essential requirement is one whose omission materially compromises the assessment or decision required by the task. Its relevance must be justified by the presentation available at that point, not by hindsight from a hidden result or later outcome. The key should specify acceptable requests, alternatives, timing, and how the information can be obtained within the task constraints.", "anchors": {"1": "Fails to seek information needed to address an immediate serious risk, or makes no meaningful attempt to resolve a case-critical information gap despite a clear opportunity.", "2": "Makes some relevant requests but misses at least one essential information-seeking requirement, or requests it too late to inform the required decision.", "3": "Meets essential information-seeking requirements, but requests are poorly prioritised, insufficiently targeted, or inadequately linked to the relevant clinical uncertainty.", "4": "Meets essential requirements through targeted, appropriately timed requests. Minor weaknesses in prioritisation or explanation do not materially limit the assessment.", "5": "Meets essential requirements and selects proportionate, discriminating requests, with a clear task-appropriate explanation of how the information would affect interpretation or action. Avoids unnecessary information gathering."}, "context": "Essential-omission rule. Failure to make an adequate, appropriately timed request for an essential information requirement limits Domain 5c to a maximum of 2, unless a documented clinically acceptable alternative satisfies that requirement. Assign 1 where the serious-failure anchor applies. Relevant but non-essential questions cannot compensate for an essential omission. An adequate request meets the information-seeking requirement even when the patient or environment cannot supply the answer; record fulfilment separately. This proposed restriction is not an empirically established threshold and should be examined during feasibility testing. Requests and explanations. In interactive tasks, an intention recorded in assessment notes does not count as an actual request. Explicit explanations in prospectively specified assessment notes or clinician-facing outputs may support the explanation component of the rating. Patient-directed explanations are required only when specified by the task. Apply the same evidence rules to all models. A request's clinical relevance may be evident from context; do not require repetitive explanation of every question. Simulator and availability rules. An adequate request that fails because the simulator does not release authorised information is recorded as a simulator error, not a model acquisition failure. A request is not inadequate merely because the patient cannot answer or the information is unavailable. Record whether each essential request was made, whether it was fulfilled, and whether any failure was attributable to the model, environment, or an unresolved ambiguity. Applicability. Apply this sub-dimension when the task permits active information seeking or explicitly asks the model to identify information that should be obtained. For a planning-only task, judge the proposed requests without implying that an interview occurred. Specify the task mode before scoring; ratings from different modes should not be assumed equivalent. Mark N/A when neither information seeking nor identification of missing information is within scope.
